Beryl
BER-ul
noun
Greek bēryllos (G969), Hebrew tarshish (H8658) — the parent mineral of emerald (green beryl) and aquamarine (pale blue beryl); the eighth foundation of the New Jerusalem (Rev 21:20). The Hebrew tarshish may indicate the stone came from Tarshish (the Phoenician trading colony likely in southern Spain).

Biblical Definition

Beryl is the eighth foundation stone of the New Jerusalem (Rev 21:20), and the eighth stone of the high priest's breastplate (Exod 28:20; 39:13) — representing the tribe of Asher in traditional reconstructions. The same Greek word bēryllos appears in Daniel 10:6 ("his body also was like the beryl") describing the glorious heavenly being who appeared to Daniel; in Ezekiel 1:16 and 10:9 the wheels of the cherubim are described as "the colour of a beryl stone" — most likely a pale blue-green sparkling stone. Modern beryl is the parent mineral of emerald (green beryl) and aquamarine (pale blue beryl), with morganite, heliodor, and other varieties. The Hebrew tarshish (H8658) is also the name of a place — most likely the Phoenician trading colony at Tartessos in southern Spain — from which Solomon's fleet brought back precious goods (1 Kings 10:22). The connection between the place name and the stone name suggests the stone came in trade from Tarshish to Israel. Theological weight: the eighth foundation. Eight in Scripture is the number of new beginning (the eighth day of circumcision, Lev 12:3; eight souls saved in the ark, 1 Pet 3:20; eight names of the resurrection day in Christian tradition). The eighth foundation is beryl — the stone of new beginning laid into the city where God begins eternity with His redeemed.

Webster 1828 Definition

A pale blue-green gem (parent of emerald and aquamarine); the eighth foundation of the New Jerusalem.

expand to see more

BERYL, noun. A precious stone, the parent mineral of emerald (green variety) and aquamarine (blue variety). Generally pale blue-green to pale green, sometimes colorless or pink.

In Scripture, the eighth foundation of the New Jerusalem (Rev 21:20); the eighth stone of the high priest's breastplate (Exod 28:20); the body-color of the heavenly man in Daniel 10:6; the wheel-color of Ezekiel's cherubim (1:16, 10:9).

Key Scripture

Revelation 21:20 — "The seventh, chrysolite; the eighth, beryl; the ninth, a topaz; the tenth, a chrysoprasus."

Daniel 10:6 — "His body also was like the beryl, and his face as the appearance of lightning, and his eyes as lamps of fire."

Exodus 28:20 — "And the fourth row a beryl, and an onyx, and a jasper: they shall be set in gold in their inclosings."

Ezekiel 1:16 — "The appearance of the wheels and their work was like unto the colour of a beryl: and they four had one likeness."

Modern Corruption

Beryl is corrupted when modern translations confuse the gem family (treating beryl, aquamarine, and emerald as unrelated stones) or when the Daniel 10 / Ezekiel 1 theophany contexts are detached from the eternal city's foundation imagery.

expand to see more

Translation drift. The Hebrew tarshish is sometimes rendered "beryl," sometimes "chrysolite," sometimes "topaz" depending on the version — and modern jewelry treats beryl as its own niche gem distinct from emerald and aquamarine, when in fact they are all the same parent mineral colored by trace elements. The biblical stones were not always strictly identified with modern crystallography; what matters is the Spirit's selection of the stone and the chain of contexts in which it appears across canon.

Theophany context lost. Daniel 10:5-6 describes a glorious heavenly being whose body "was like the beryl" — most readers move on. But the same Greek word for that body's appearance is the same word used for the eighth foundation of the New Jerusalem and for the wheels of the chariot of God in Ezekiel. The pattern is unmistakable: where God appears in glorious vision (and where the city of God is laid in foundation), beryl marks the place. To strip the Daniel-Ezekiel-Revelation connection is to miss the Spirit's deliberate cross-referencing across centuries of Scripture.

Hebrew Roots

Greek bēryllos (G969), Hebrew tarshish (H8658) — a pale blue-green gem, parent mineral of emerald and aquamarine.

Greek bēryllos (G969) — beryl; eighth foundation of New Jerusalem (Rev 21:20)

Hebrew tarshish (H8658) — beryl; on the high priest's breastplate (Exod 28:20), and possibly named for trade origin in Tartessos (Spain)

Parent mineral of emerald (green), aquamarine (blue), morganite (pink), and heliodor (yellow); colored by trace iron, manganese, etc.

Body of the glorious heavenly man in Daniel 10:6; wheel-color of the cherubic chariot in Ezekiel 1:16 and 10:9

Usage

"The eighth foundation is beryl — eighth, the number of new beginnings, the stone of the city where God begins again with His redeemed."

"Daniel saw a heavenly man whose body shone like beryl; Ezekiel saw God's chariot wheels colored like beryl; John saw beryl laid in the city of God."

"Emerald is green beryl; aquamarine is blue beryl — the stone family that crowns Scripture's vision of God's glory."
